- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% in early spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.67) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% in early dips.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., >5.0) — cap forecast at 20–30% above true peak for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >2.5σ above recent mean, adjust downward by 15–25%.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with forecast instability — smooth forecasts by averaging 3–5 prior days if sentiment shifts >0.33.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) for 5+ days, model tends to lag — add 0.1–0.2 to forecast for next 3–7 days.
- Forecast errors are more severe in early days of 30-day horizon — apply 15–20% correction for day 1–5 if sentiment is weak or negative.
